symptom: The nightly goes red on the Mendix 11.14.0 and 11.15.0 legs only, in `TestRunLifecycle_DetachStatusExecWaitStop`: `wait (Mendix 11.14+): want build #2 to fail with the serve-rebuild hint; exit 0, "applied: build #2 via restart in 48.1s (runtime restarted; browser sessions dropped)"`. Every other leg, push CI and the unit tests are green
cause: Not a product defect: a nightly-only test pinned the 11.14+ mxbuild --serve regression as a FAILED build #2, and cf135bfc (serveRecovery) made the watch loop restart mxbuild --serve and build on the fresh process when an incremental build fails for want of client source, so build #2 now applies. The lifecycle test needs a cached mxbuild and a runtime, so it runs only in the nightly matrix, never in the PR that changed the behaviour
insight: A test that pins a documented failure is a contract with the code that explains it: improving that failure flips the test, and when the test only runs nightly the flip lands a day later on main. Whoever changes serve_recovery.go, webclient_legacy_paths.go or the watch loop should grep for `serveRebuildsBroken` and run the lifecycle test on 11.14+. The new assertion keeps the 'when mxbuild fixes it, this branch should go' property by requiring the recovery's own log line ('cannot build this change incrementally') next to the applied build, not just an applied build. Reproduce in about 2 minutes: `mxcli setup mxbuild --version 11.14.0`, JAVA_HOME at a JDK 25 (11.14's serve refuses 21 with 'JDK 25 not found'), then `MXCLI_RUNLIFE_VERSION=11.14.0 go test -tags integration -run TestRunLifecycle_DetachStatusExecWaitStop ./cmd/mxcli/`. Controls: the old test against current code fails at line 157 with the nightly's exact message; the new test passes all six steps; the new test with the legacy-client restart branch stubbed fails with mxbuild's 'Could not find a part of the path …/web/pages/MyFirstModule.Hello.js'
